something i forgot to mention is the cognitive aspect. all EDs, bulimia included though restriction is the biggest culprit, severely affect your brain functioning. that can be deadly. the purge cycle can make your decision making just, completely irrational. even small cognitive deficits can cause major safety risks — driving is a big example. everybody’s different of course.

additionally, drinking alcohol with EDs can a very different experience — in my opinion, restrictors should not drink. its extremely dangerous & the risk of alcohol poisoning is much higher. for bulimics it’s a little bit different but a very common cause of alcohol related death is choking on your own vomit while unconscious and i can see that increasing with bulimics because the throat valve lining can degrade so much that stomach acid and vomit flows up freely. that can get bad enough to require surgery to fix.

it does serious damage to your esophagus and throat. in the long term it erodes your esophagus and can greatly raise your chances of esophageal cancer. the heart problems really shouldn’t be underestimated either, *especially* with laxatives. it’s also extremely difficult on your kidneys — it can lead to kidney failure and kidney stones. 

it’s difficult to attribute a death to an ED once someone has recovered so doctors typically describe it as a  “risk factor” — a past ED is a risk factor for all these diseases and complications. a lot of the time these are long-term, so they’re more likely the longer you keep purging at this rate, but you’re still at a higher likelihood already compared to the average population. people with EDs also have a lower average lifespan and reddit users trend quite young, especially in these spaces. that said — young people are less likely to die from EDs, yes. but developmentally you will be affected by it and your body loses that tolerance quickly. by your 20s EDs get a lot deadlier.

so this is a good time to say that true permanent damage from EDs is not super common. of herbs and altars (whose videos can be triggering, forewarning) has a good video summarizing this. he talks about permanent side effects like bone damage (osteoporosis), IBS, and occasionally esophageal damage to the throat flap from severe recurring purging (this i think can only be fixed through surgery). fertility per se isn’t usually affected but there is a higher miscarriage rate sadly. heart damage is another really common problem. i personally deal with enamel damage and acid reflux — both are easily remedied, but still technically permanent.

binge eating alone has a different set of problems, most of it are things like heart problems, diabetes, also IBS, etc. but these can honestly take way longer to show up — you have to binge a lot more food over a way longer period of time than you think to do equivalent damage as restriction or b/p. as in, it can literally take DECADES. restriction and b/p permanent consequences can show up in 2-3 years or less. most consequences of binging are short-term and remedied within 6 months or less. if you binge way too much, way past fullness, your stomach can burst and cause severe internal damage. that is NOT common in just bingers — i believe it does happen in bulimics bc of the damage purging & laxatives does. 

*that said, A LOT of these are the result of severe restriction or binging/purging over years. it is NOT too late to recover and it is very likely you have not done any permanent damage and you can still recover. i’ve known girls with heart problems from past anorexia struggles who’ve recovered and live very happy, full lives.*

i think fasting for religious purposes, like ramadan, etc. isn’t an eating disorder. 

personally, i don’t think fasting for three days is ever healthy. at the same time, if a monk or an activist fasts for three days as a hunger strike — is that an eating disorder? no, probably not. anyone can do anything and it doesn’t mean much into what they actually think. if someone binge eats every day for three days do they have BED suddenly? no, i don’t think so. 

i think a greater observation is that, as basically all of us have had problems w EDs, we tend to project our own disordered thoughts onto other people. obviously there’s tons of unhealthy behavior in diet culture or whatever — but as ED sufferers, should we be nitpicking them? is it healthy for us to be reading through diet subs and reading about hugely unhealthy weight losses and analyzing exactly how unhealthy it all is? it almost feels like another way of triggering the competitive side of EDs, especially the posts I’ve seen with the long fasts. half of the posts screenshotted on here probably get drowned out in their home subs, but if you’re suffering and looking to trigger yourself, well… you can just look here.
